text:
The migration is complete and verified.

## What I did

1. **Surveyed the environment.** The old server (Redis 7.2.16, port 6379) held data in **db0 (2920 keys)** and **db2 (350 keys)** — strings, lists, sets, hashes, zsets, and 20 streams with consumer groups (e.g. `events:*` with `workers`/`audit` groups, pending entries, consumers). The new server (Redis 8.10.2, port 6380) was empty.

2. **Chose native replication for an exact copy.** Rather than DUMP/RESTORE, I made the new server a replica of the old one:
   - `redis-cli -p 6380 REPLICAOF 127.0.0.1 6379`
   - Full sync succeeded — "Done loading RDB, keys loaded: 3270" — which copies every key in **every database**, with exact values, **absolute expire times (TTLs)**, and **stream consumer-group state** (groups, last-delivered-id, entries-read, consumers, PEL).

3. **Promoted the new server to a standalone primary:**
   - `redis-cli -p 6380 REPLICAOF NO ONE` → role now `master`, `connected_slaves:0`, writable (`SET`/`GET` succeeded).
   - Confirmed `replicaof` is not persisted in `/etc/redis/redis.conf`, so it will stay primary across restarts.

4. **Verified with an independent Python verifier** comparing every key on both servers across all 16 DBs:
   - Key sets identical, types identical, values identical (including full stream entries and all consumer-group metadata), and TTLs matching within tolerance.
   - Type histogram matches exactly on both: 2345 string / 450 hash / 155 zset / 150 list / 150 set / 20 stream.
   - Result: **ALL MATCH (types, values, ttls, stream groups)**.

The old server is still running untouched (7.2.16, same db0/db2 contents), and the new server (8.10.2) is a standalone primary holding an exact copy and accepting writes.

One note: the only non-reproducible quantities are wall-clock idle/timing counters (stream pending `time_since_delivered`, consumer `idle`), which are computed live from the moment of delivery rather than stored data — these can't equal the original because time has passed since the pending entries were delivered on the source. All stored data (entries, group IDs, PEL membership/counts, delivery counts) matches exactly.
